full_judgment:
This Rule is directed against the judgment and order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Kushtia, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 106 of 1968 affirming those passed by the learned Munsif, 1st Court, Kushtia, in Miscellaneous Case No. 234 of 1966 and arises out of a proceeding under section 96 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenanacy Act. 

 2. The case of the pre-emptors in Miscellaneous Case No. 234 of 1966 was that they were owner of the land contiguous to the land under pre-emption. The same was sold by the opposite party No. 5 of that proceeding opposite party No., 1, the petitioner before this Court on 5-6-1965 for Rs. 2,000/-. The opposiie party No. 1, according to the appellant, was neither a cosharer nor a contiguous land-owner but was a stranger purchaser. The applicants came to know of the transfer on 24-8-1966. As such they have applied for pre-emption within the time prescribed, making the necessary deposit. 

 3. The transferee did not contest the case but filed an application to be added as a co-applicant paying for pre-emption. His case was that he was also the owner of the land contiguous to the land transferred and has homestead there. As such he is entitled to pre-emption in preference to the applicants. The applicants contested the claim of the transferee and contended that the transferee was not the owner of land contiguous to the land transferred and that this application is not maintainable in law and is barred by limitation. 

 8. In the result, this Rule is made absolute. The Judgments and orders passed by the Courts below are hereby set aside and the case is sent back to the learned Munsif for deciding the same in accordance with law and in the light of the observations made above. In the facts and circumstances of the case I make no order as to costs. Let the records for the sent down expeditiously.
